choices: The guard insisted to check every bag at the gate.
The new clerk is capable of handling the payroll.
The residents had to cope up with the water shortage.
Ms. Cruz graduated in a state university in 2018.
answer: The new clerk is capable of handling the payroll.
hints: Each sentence has a verb or a describing word followed by a small linking word (a preposition). Only one pair is standard English.
Say each pair on its own: "insisted to", "capable of", "cope up with", "graduated in (a school)". Which ones are standard fixed pairs?

Test each sentence with three questions. Does the word need a preposition + -ing verb instead of "to" + verb? Is there an extra word that adds nothing? Is it the right preposition after "graduate" and a school? The sentence that passes all three tests is correct.

steps.action: Check "insisted to check". "Insist" pairs with "on" and an -ing verb: "insisted on checking". This sentence is wrong.
Check "capable of handling". "Capable" pairs with "of" and an -ing verb. This sentence is correct.
steps.why: "Capable of" means "able to". You say "capable of doing", not "capable to do".

steps.action: Check "cope up with". The standard phrase is "cope with", with no "up". This sentence is wrong.
steps.why: "Cope up" is common in the Philippines, but it is not standard English.

steps.action: Check "graduated in a state university". You graduate from a school. This sentence is wrong.
steps.why: The second "in" ("in 2018") is fine, because "in" goes with a year.

steps.action: The correct sentence is "The new clerk is capable of handling the payroll."

trapNotes.The guard insisted to check every bag at: "Insist to" follows the pattern of "want to", so it sounds natural. But "insist" takes "on": "insisted on checking every bag".
trapNotes.The residents had to cope up with the wa: "Cope up with" is very common in Philippine English, but the standard phrase is just "cope with".
trapNotes.Ms. Cruz graduated in a state university: "In" seems right for a place, but with "graduate" the partner word is "from": "graduated from a state university".
